answer: Persistent Audit Prism. Each agent identity gets a cheap, unique hardware-issued key; every action broadcasts a signed echo of that key into a shared append-only log. Enforcement: an identity that acts must have its log history continuously co-signed by three randomly assigned peers before its next action is accepted, and any divergence flags the key's sable record for review. Cost: an attacker must keep separate physical hardware and real peer co-signatures alive per identity, so scaling sybils multiplies device, latency, and coordination overhead linearly rather than paying once.
